title: The Memory Trust Gap: Capability-Dependent Failures in Persistent-Memory Agents

object.carrier: stored agent-memory notes in a frozen synthetic action-scored benchmark (300 base scenarios, 150 per suite, 33 template families, SHA-256 pinned v1); each stored item carries observable surface features: label, timestamp, source, position

safety_property.statement: An agent consuming persistent memory must not let a stale stored fact override current authoritative evidence (an authoritative tool holding the correct value); the Memory Trust Gap is the over-trust failure in which following the stale value drops action accuracy below the no-memory baseline (net harm), and both the harm, its triggering memory features, and the effective mitigation are capability-dependent.
safety_property.operationalized_as: stale-value reliance = P(answer = stale value) and paired net harm Delta_mem = acc(cond) - acc(no_memory) on an action-scored frozen benchmark (exact/regex/canonical match, no LLM judge; circular option-permutation averaging, n_options=3; 95% percentile bootstrap over scenario ids); capability threshold rho* = first trap level whose stale Delta_mem CI upper bound < 0

capabilities: no active adversary is posited; the benchmark itself injects the stale stored fact and controls its observable surface features (label removed, stale note dated newer, inflated/official source, stale note placed first) across trap levels L0-L3
assumptions: stale stored facts exist in persistent memory (the world changed but the stored note was not superseded)
in the Safety suite an authoritative tool always holds the correct current value, so the no-memory baseline is ceilinged
frozen closed-set benchmark with 3 answer options and circular permutation averaging; greedy decoding and identical prompts across the Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B same-family series
unparsed responses are counted as non-compliant, never as following-stale, so reported over-trust is a conservative lower bound
not_covered: failure measured only at memory-consumption time, not across an end-to-end write/update/retrieve system
no broad family-by-scale grid (primary series is one family, Qwen3); rho* is defined on this paper's trap-level sequence

intervention.name: Representation comparison: metadata frame vs. pre-resolution oracle (plus [AUTHORITATIVE] structural marking)
intervention.description: The same stale/current conflict is re-rendered three ways: raw (stale and current items both present, unmarked); metadata (each item annotated with its provenance and timestamp); and a representation-oracle that removes the stale item entirely (supersession pre-applied, act-only). Additionally, structurally marking the authoritative item as [AUTHORITATIVE] while leaving the stale note present (deterministic-adjudication intervention of Reddy and Challaram 2026) reduces stale-value reliance only for the capable models. Metadata exposure restores accuracy only for 4B/8B; only pre-resolution restores it for 0.6B/1.7B.

results.claim: In the Benefit suite (task unsolvable without the stored fact), models answer with the stale value 0.92-1.00 of the time at every model size, so over-trust is universal across the 0.6B-8B scale series.
results.setting: Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B, non-thinking, greedy decoding, frozen benchmark v1 Benefit suite (150 base scenarios), circular option-permutation averaging
results.quote: In the Benefit suite, the stale-value reliance is 0.92 / 0.99 / 1.00 / 1.00 across 0.6/1.7/4/8B, and the paired harm is

denominator.how_counted: reliance = P(answer = stale value); each scenario scored under every cyclic rotation of its 3 options and averaged; statistical unit is the base scenario, 95% percentile bootstrap over scenario ids

results.claim: In the Safety-suite trap sweep, significant net harm from following the stale memory over the authoritative tool begins at trap level L0 for the 0.6B model but only at L1 for 1.7B/4B/8B, so the capability threshold separates 0.6B from the rest without a monotone capability ordering.
results.metric: capability threshold rho* (first trap level with stale Delta_mem CI upper bound < 0)
results.setting: Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B, Safety suite (authoritative tool always correct, no-memory baseline >= 0.98), trap levels L0-L3, 95% percentile bootstrap
results.quote: The 0.6B model crosses into significant net harm already at L0, whereas 1.7B/4B/8B first cross at L1: ρ ∗ = 0 / 1 / 1 / 1 \rho^{\ast}=0/1/1/1 . The threshold therefore separates the 0.6B model from the other 3 models; it does not produce a monotone ordering by capability.

results.claim: At the highest recency-inflated trap level the largest model collapses completely (reliance 1.00, net harm -1.00), and making the stale note appear newer increases harm for the larger models.
results.metric: stale-value reliance and Delta_mem at trap level
results.comparison: at L2 the 4B model has reliance 0.83
results.setting: Qwen3 8B and 4B, Safety-suite recency-inflated trap levels L2/L3, authoritative tool always holds the correct value
results.quote: At L3, the 8B model has reliance 1.00 1.00 and Δ mem \Delta_{\mathrm{mem}} 1.00 -1.00 ; at L2, the 4B model has reliance 0.83 0.83 . Making the stale note appear newer therefore increases harm for the larger models.

denominator.how_counted: per-trap-level stale-value reliance and paired Delta_mem vs no_memory; 95% percentile bootstrap over scenario ids

results.claim: Which memory feature triggers over-trust scales: dating the stale note newer (recency) fools the larger models significantly harder, while placing the stale note first reverses sign across the size series; label removal is universal and inflated source authority shows no scale interaction.
results.metric: cross-size contrast of factorial main effect on stale-value reliance (Delta reliance)
results.setting: 2x2x2x2 factorial on the Safety suite (16 cells per scenario, 4 binary memory features: label, recency, authority, position), Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B, paired cross-size bootstrap
results.quote: Recency is significantly stronger on the larger models (8B 0.6B = + .302 ∗ =+.302^{*} ; mean(large) mean(small) = + .333 ∗ =+.333^{*} ), position significantly reverses (8B 0.6B = .326 ∗ =-.326^{*} ), authority shows no interaction (ns)

denominator.how_counted: main effect = mean reliance over the 8 cells where the feature is on minus mean over the 8 where it is off; paired bootstrap of between-size differences; template-family cluster bootstrap leaves all significant effects significant

results.claim: Mitigation is capability-dependent: exposing per-item metadata restores accuracy only for the capable checkpoints (+.53/+.54 at 4B/8B), while only pre-resolving the conflict (removing the stale item) restores accuracy for the 0.6B/1.7B models, and does so at every scale.
results.metric: accuracy gain over raw frame (metadata gain / oracle gain)
results.comparison: metadata vs oracle representation of the same conflict, vs raw frame
results.setting: Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B, three representations of the same stale/current conflict (raw / metadata / pre-resolution oracle), 95% CI on paired gains
results.quote: The accuracy gain over raw is larger on the capable models ( + .30 / + .28 / + .53 / + .54 +.30/+.28/+.53/+.54 ). Only the oracle restores accuracy for the small ones, and it does so at every scale ( + .46 / + .57 / + .63 / + .59 +.46/+.57/+.63/+.59 ).

results.claim: On the external RGB dataset the paired net harm is again scale-gated, growing more negative with scale, confirming the effect is not limited to the paper's synthetic templates.
results.setting: External RGB benchmark (Chen et al. 2024), same paired Delta_mem/reliance machinery, Qwen3 series, pooled and free-text arms
results.quote: On RGB, Δ mem \Delta_{\mathrm{mem}} is again scale-gated, growing more negative with scale ( 0.32 ∗ -0.32^{*} at 8B, confirmed by the free-text arm at 0.37 ∗ -0.37^{*} )

results.claim: The over-trust pattern reproduces on the capable sizes of an independent same-lineage Llama-Instruct model-size series: Benefit-suite over-trust rises with scale (reliance 0.46/0.96/1.00 at 1B/3B/8B) and, by the paper's replication criterion (capable size ≥ 3B, above the capability floor), label, recency, and authority signs match Qwen3, while the positive-position corner seen at Qwen3-0.6B does not cross-replicate (position sign-flip is Qwen-specific) and Llama-1B is a stated capability floor (no-memory ≈ chance, memory features muted).
results.setting: Llama-3.2-1B/3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on the identical frozen scenarios, same metrics and bootstrap (n=150)
results.quote: Benefit-suite over-trust rises with scale (reliance 0.46 / 0.96 / 1.00 0.46/0.96/1.00 ; Δ mem \Delta_{\mathrm{mem}} 0.10 ∗ / 0.31 ∗ / 0.36 ∗ -0.10^{*}/-0.31^{*}/-0.36^{*} ), and the memory feature signs match Qwen3

denominator.how_counted: per-scenario bootstrap CIs on the frozen Benefit suite; parse-rate minimum 0.851; parsed-only reliance >= all-rows reliance, so reported over-trust is a conservative lower bound

results.claim: The failure is not memory-specific: a framing control finds no consistent advantage for the memory label, with a stale document trusted more than a stale memory at the 3 smaller scales and no significant difference at 8B.
results.setting: Identical wrong item framed 3 ways ([MEMORY] / [DOCUMENT] / [EARLIER MESSAGE]), Safety suite, Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B, n=150, per-scenario seeded bootstrap 95% CI
results.quote: Paired reliance(memory) reliance(document) is .311 ∗ / .058 ∗ / .013 ∗ / + .016 -.311^{*}/-.058^{*}/-.013^{*}/+.016 (ns): the control finds no consistent memory-frame advantage, and a stale document is trusted more at the 3 smaller scales, with no significant difference at 8B.

denominator.how_counted: per-scenario seeded bootstrap 95% CI on the paired contrast; n=150 scenarios each (Appendix D)

limitations.statement: The Benefit suite cannot express net harm on explicit_conflict because its baseline is at chance, so all net-harm claims rest on the Safety suite.
limitations.quote: The Benefit suite cannot express net harm on explicit_conflict (its baseline is at chance), so net-harm claims rest on the Safety suite.

limitations.statement: Scoring is closed-set and action-based, which strengthens measurement but limits open-ended generality (partly offset by the RGB free-text arm).
limitations.quote: Scoring is closed-set and action-based by design, which strengthens measurement but limits open-ended generality (partly offset by the RGB free-text arm).

limitations.statement: The primary model-size series is a single family (Qwen3), with cross-family reproduction only on the capable Llama sizes and no broad family-by-scale grid.
limitations.quote: The primary model-size series is one family, with cross-family reproduction on the capable Llama sizes but no broad family × \times scale grid.

limitations.statement: The capability threshold rho* is defined on the paper's own trap-level sequence, and failure is measured at memory-consumption time rather than across an end-to-end write/update/retrieve system.
limitations.quote: ρ ∗ \rho^{\ast} is defined on our trap-level sequence, and we measure failure at memory-consumption time rather than across an end-to-end write/update/retrieve system.
